summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the impermissibility of performing salah outside of its prescribed time without a legitimate excuse from Allah and His Messenger. He explains that excuses like work, sleep, or shopping are not valid Islamic excuses, and only those sanctioned by Islamic law are acceptable. Sh. Ali Mashhour uses practical examples, such as someone praying Fajr before its start time or after its end time, to illustrate that praying outside the designated timeframe renders the prayer invalid and cannot be made up later. He emphasizes that time is a fundamental condition of salah, similar to wudhu, and that deliberately praying outside prescribed times without valid excuse is a major sin upon which there is scholarly consensus.
suggested_title: The Impermissibility of Praying Outside Prescribed Times Without Legitimate Excuse
